hero.title_html: All Islamic Knowledge Sources, in One Interface.
hero.lede: Stop juggling dozens of independent MCP servers. Connect @IslamicSources once to Gemini, Claude Desktop, Cursor, or Antigravity and access Quran, Hadith, Tafsir, and Islamic heritage books. As a neutral aggregator, we relay upstream responses verbatim without alteration, provided 'as is'.
hero.note_text: Powered by Cloudflare Workers with zero local installation
hero.disclaimer_text: @IslamicSources operates strictly as an aggregator. We do not add, edit, or alter responses from upstream Islamic sources; all data is transmitted verbatim and provided 'as is'.

config.title: Configure Your AI Assistant in One Minute.
config.subtitle: Select your AI client or web assistant and follow the simple setup steps.
config.dev_notice_desc: Cloudflare WAF automatically blocks generic client User-Agents (such as default Python-urllib). Always provide a custom User-Agent header (e.g. User-Agent: my-app/1.0.0) in your programmatic requests.
config.guide_claude: Add a custom connector in Claude
config.caveat_claude: A free account allows one custom connector; on Team and Enterprise plans an owner adds it first.
config.caveat_chatgpt: Plugin availability depends on your account and workspace permissions.
config.caveat_gemini: Custom apps are added from your account's connected apps page.
claude_web_steps: Set Name to 'Islamic Sources (@IslamicSources)' and Server URL to 'https://mcp.waqf.app/mcp'.
Click 'Add' to save (public open waqf endpoint, no OAuth required).
In any chat, click the '+' icon next to the message composer, choose 'Connectors', and toggle Islamic Sources ON.
chatgpt_web_steps: Enable Developer Mode: Open chatgpt.com, click your profile in the bottom-left corner, select Settings → Security and login, and switch 'Developer mode' On.
Navigate to Plugins: Open chatgpt.com/plugins (or Settings → Plugins in the left sidebar), click Browse plugins, then click the '+' (plus) icon near the top-right search box.

Enter MCP Details: Set Name: 'Islamic Sources (@IslamicSources)', Description: 'Federated Islamic Knowledge & MCP Gateway', Connection: 'Server URL', Server URL: 'https://mcp.waqf.app/mcp', and Authentication: 'None'.
Authorize: Check the box 'I understand and want to continue' to bypass the unverified connector warning, then click 'Create'.

Use in Chat: Start a fresh new conversation (existing chats will not recognize newly added plugins), select Islamic Sources as source or prompt 'What tools do you have available?' to query Quran, Hadith, and Turath.
gemini_web_steps: Under 'Connected Apps', click 'Add a custom app'.
Set Name to 'IslamicSources' and Endpoint URL to 'https://mcp.waqf.app/mcp'.
Save and authorize the connected custom app.
In Gemini chat, invoke tools naturally using @IslamicSources (e.g. '@IslamicSources search tafsir of Ayat al-Kursi').
config.config_note: Tip: Use '?suite=core' to expose only canonical tools and conserve token budget.

prompts.title: Start With a Question, Let the Assistant Read the Source.
prompts.subtitle: Paste one into your chat, and name the gateway before your question.
prompts.card1_body: Search Aljam3 for passages about intention (niyyah) in worship. Read the surrounding pages, explain the text simply, and cite the book, author and page number with a source link.
prompts.card2_body: Find books on the principles of Islamic jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh) in Aljam3. Show their authors and source libraries, then help me choose a passage to study with its references.
prompts.card3_body: Check important quotations against the PDF. Extracted text may contain errors, and file page numbers can differ from printed page numbers. Keep your explanation distinct from the author's words.
prompts.caveat_ocr: Automatically extracted text may contain errors; verify important quotations against the original PDF.
prompts.caveat_pagination: Page numbers refer to the digitized file and can differ from the printed edition.
prompts.caveat_attribution: Keep the assistant's explanation distinct from the author's words, and cite the book, author, page and source link.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: Why use mcp.waqf.dev instead of individual MCP servers?
faq.a1: A single configuration eliminates managing 10+ server endpoints, prevents tool name collisions, caches authentic texts at the edge, and provides canonical tools that save context window tokens.
faq.a2: Yes, this gateway is 100% open-source and endowed as a digital waqf for public benefit. Please note that we do not own, manage, or operate the independent MCP servers federated in our aggregator, nor are we affiliated with their operations. Furthermore, the Waqf Digital Public License (Waqf-DPL) applies strictly to the gateway aggregator software and technical infrastructure, not to the underlying Islamic content or texts. Each federated MCP server retains its own independent license and terms of use, which must be verified directly at the source.
faq.a3: We do not store private API keys or personal prompts. Anonymized operational telemetry (country, tool called, response latency) is recorded strictly for health and capacity monitoring.
faq.q4: Does @IslamicSources add, edit, or alter responses from the sources?
faq.a4: No. @IslamicSources operates strictly as an aggregator and neutral edge gateway. We do not author, add to, edit, or alter any response or text received from connected Islamic providers. All content is relayed verbatim and the service is provided strictly on an 'as is' basis without warranties.
faq.q5: Does the gateway support MCP Resources and Prompts in addition to Tools?
faq.a5: Yes. The gateway provides full MCP protocol coverage. Alongside the federated specialized tools, it exposes direct catalog resources (quran://surahs, quran://tafsirs, quran://sciences, quran://schema) for browsing Quran and tafsir data, plus standardized prompt templates for studying, comparing and explaining verses, with Cloudflare D1 edge caching.
